name: Pilchard fishcakes
summary: Soft-centred, crisp-edged fishcakes made from one tin of pilchards in tomato sauce, with onion, carrot and parsley.
about: Tinned pilchards are a pantry staple in South African homes, and turning one tin into a plate of fishcakes is how many families stretch it for Fish Friday. Mashed with egg, onion, a little flour and oats, the fish and its tomato sauce fry up soft inside and golden outside.
steps: Tip the pilchards and their sauce into a bowl and mash with a fork. The soft bones crush easily and are good for you; lift out the spines if your family prefers.

Add the onion, carrot, eggs, flour, baking powder, oats, parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper and mix to a thick, soft batter that holds its shape on a spoon. If it is runny, stir in 1–2 tbsp more oats and leave it for 5 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat until it shimmers.

Drop in heaped tablespoons of the mixture, about 6 at a time, and flatten each to 1.5 cm thick. Fry for 3–4 minutes a side, until deep golden and firm when pressed in the middle. Add the rest of the oil for the second batch.
Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with mashed potato, peas and tomato sauce or chutney, and lemon wedges.
